title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 identifies immuno-hot tumors suggesting angiotensin-(1–7) as a sensitizer for chemotherapy
author: Mei, Cai, et al.
materials: cell lines were purchased from KeyGEN BioTECH (Nanjing, China). MDA-MB-231 cells were maintained in Leibovitz’s L-15 medium (KeyGEN BioTECH, Nanjing, China) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Hyclone, Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA) at 37 °C with 5% CO

All experiments were performed with mycoplasma-free cells. MDA-MB-231 cell lines have been authenticated using short tandem repeat profiling. The ACE2 overexpression plasmid were synthesized by KeyGEN BioTECH (Nanjing, China). The cloning vector for ACE2 overexpression plasmid was pcDNA3.1( +)-EGFP. For subsequent assays, MDA-MB-231 cells were transfected with ACE2 plasmid (2.5 μg) using Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

Cells were plated in 35-mm dishes (6 × 105 cells/dish). 48 h after transfection, all cells were harvested the proteins with lysis buffer. SDS–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and Western blotting analysis were performed as standard protocols. For nuclear and cytoplasmic protein extraction, nuclear and cytoplasmic Protein Extraction Kit were used (KeyGEN BioTECH, Nanjing, China). The primary antibodies for ACE2 (1:1000 dilution, Cat. ab15348, Abcam), PD-L1 (1:1000 dilution, Cat. 17,952–1-AP, ProteinTech) and Tubulin (1:2000 dilution, Cat. 10,094–1-AP, ProteinTech) were used. Expression levels of proteins were normalized to Tubulin for each sample.

steps.title: Pan‑cancer immunological correlation
steps.instruction: Collect expression levels of 122 immunomodulators and immune‑checkpoint genes, then compute their correlations with ACE2; use the TISIDB tool to estimate immune‑cell infiltration levels and assess correlations between ACE2 expression and infiltration.

steps.title: Linked Omics functional enrichment
steps.instruction: Access the Linked Omics web portal and predict ACE2 functional roles in breast cancer by Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway enrichment using Gene Set Enrichment Analysis with all default parameters.

steps.title: Retrieve immunophenoscore values
steps.instruction: Download breast‑cancer patient immunophenoscore (IPS) data from the Cancer Immunome Atlas (TCIA) website.

steps.title: Culture breast cancer cell lines
steps.instruction: Maintain MDA‑MB‑231 (RRID: CVCL_0062) in Leibovitz’s L‑15 medium supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; maintain 4T1 (RRID: CVCL_0125) in DMEM with 10 % FBS at the same conditions; confirm all cultures are mycoplasma‑free and authenticate MDA‑MB‑231 by short‑tandem‑repeat profiling.

steps.title: Transfect MDA‑MB‑231 with ACE2 plasmid
steps.instruction: Seed 6 × 10⁵ MDA‑MB‑231 cells per 35‑mm dish; after cells adhere, transfect with 2.5 µg ACE2 overexpression plasmid (pcDNA3.1(+)-EGFP, synthesized by KeyGEN BioTECH) using Lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions; incubate for 48 h.

steps.title: Harvest cells and extract proteins
steps.instruction: At 48 h post‑transfection, lyse cells with appropriate lysis buffer; for separate nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions, use the KeyGEN nuclear and cytoplasmic Protein Extraction Kit.

steps.title: SDS‑PAGE and Western blot
steps.instruction: Run extracted proteins on SDS‑polyacrylamide gels, transfer to membranes, and probe with primary antibodies: ACE2 (1:1000, Cat. ab15348, Abcam), PD‑L1 (1:1000, Cat. 17,952‑1‑AP, ProteinTech), and Tubulin (1:2000, Cat. 10,094‑1‑AP, ProteinTech); normalize target protein signals to Tubulin.

steps.title: Statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data in R version 4.0.0; compare two groups with parametric Student’s t‑test or non‑parametric Mann‑Whitney test, multiple groups with one‑way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s post‑hoc test, and assess correlations with Pearson analysis; consider P < 0.05 significant and annotate results with * (P < 0.05), ** (P < 0.01), *** (P < 0.001), **** (P < 0.0001).
